title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
abstract: arXiv:2611.22069v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. We release \textbf{MedGuardBench}, a drug-disjoint benchmark of 5{,}001 scenarios across 87 medications. We find that standard guardrails rely on surface cues, such as wording and profile presence, rather than patient facts. To address this, we develop \textit{personalized reasoning guardrails} with three components. \textbf{Personalized Reasoning Distillation} links risks to relevant patient fields. \textbf{Context Unrolling (CU)} makes models check each field themselves, reducing false alarms on most backbones; controls show that providing the check does not yield the same benefit. translated_title: MedGuardBench：一个面向患者的个性化防护栏开发基准
translated_abstract: 安全是因人而异的：同一个行为对一个人可能安全，对另一个人却可能不安全。然而，当前的防护栏在判断内容时并未考虑受影响的是谁。我们以用药安全为切入点，提出了“以患者为条件的用药防护”，即根据患者档案和处方来预测安全判定结果以及17个风险类别。我们发布了MedGuardBench，这是一个涵盖87种药物、包含5,001个场景且训练与测试药物互不重叠的基准数据集。我们发现，标准防护栏依赖的是表层线索（如措辞和患者档案是否存在），而非患者的真实信息。为解决这一问题，我们开发了由三个组件构成的个性化推理防护栏。个性化推理蒸馏将风险与相关的患者字段关联起来。上下文展开让模型自行逐项检查各个患者字段，在大多数骨干模型上降低了误报率；对照实验表明，直接向模型提供检查结果并不能带来同样的收益。一种基于规则的……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文发布了MedGuardBench——首个以患者档案和处方为条件的个性化用药安全防护基准（包含87种药物、5,001个场景），并提出个性化推理防护栏方法，使模型能够基于患者的真实信息而非表面线索做出安全判断。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MedGuardBench, a patient-conditioned medication safety benchmark with 5,001 scenarios across 87 drugs, and develops personalized reasoning guardrails that make safety judgments based on actual patient facts rather than surface cues.
